run.change_description: fix(vercel): Fix ISR path rewrite to prevent 404

summary.intent: Restore ISR-served routes after #15959 by rewriting the request path from the ISR query parameter, so ISR pages stop returning 404.
summary.issue_fit: Partial: the rewrite is implemented, but that Vercel sends the trigger header and does not let clients forge it could not be checked offline. No issue was supplied; the pull-request text is the only intent source.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed; scratch in-process test on the built _render function at the reviewed head; the repository's own tests could not run in place because the clone was read-only in the shell; Vercel platform behaviour unavailable.
check_details: Reviewer-executed at the reviewed head: scratch node test (clone-work/spoof.test.mjs, fixture copied to clone-work/fx) calling the built _render handler in-process. Result: with `x-vercel-isr: 1` a request for `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` is served as `private`; without the header, or with `x-vercel-isr: 0`, as `public`.

Environmental failure, not a test failure: `node --test test/path-override-security.test.js` in the clone failed at fixture build with `Read-only file system` writing `.astro/collections`; the change adds or edits no tests, so nothing depends on it.
Unavailable: the author's manual Vercel deployments and any Vercel platform behaviour (header handling, ISR cache).

questions.title: Can a client forge the `x-vercel-isr` header that now authorizes the path override?
questions.evidence: `entrypoint.ts` now rewrites the pathname from the `x_astro_path` query parameter whenever no middleware secret is present and `x-vercel-isr` is `1`. The same entrypoint backs `_render` in every serverless build, and nothing in the repository sets or checks that header. The reviewer's in-process test served `/api/private` from `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` on the built `_render` function when the header was sent; the existing security tests do not send it. Whether Vercel strips or overwrites a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` before the function runs could not be established offline.
questions.why_it_matters: If Vercel passes a client-supplied header through, this reopens the authorization bypass that #15959 closed: a caller reaches any route through `_render` without the edge middleware. That would be a must-fix security finding. If the platform always overwrites the header, the change stands.
questions.answer: Vercel documentation or a deployed test that sends `x-vercel-isr: 1` from an external client to a route or `/_render` can settle it. A maintainer familiar with the platform can also confirm. Either way, a regression test in `path-override-security.test.js` for the header case is worth adding.

requirements.source: pr-body/"made any route served by ISR result in a 404"
requirements.evidence: entrypoint.ts:24-25 maps x_astro_path to the pathname when x-vercel-isr is 1, which matches the ISR route dest in index.ts:63; whether Vercel sends that header to the _isr function is a platform fact that could not be checked offline.
The cited deployments are external and were not reachable offline; the reviewer's in-process test shows only that the rewrite works when the header is present.
